messages:
Sarah: Hey @Omar — I added my spouse during open enrollment but they were abroad and coverage start was set to 2026-05-01. They returned earlier; can the coverage be backdated to 2026-04-01? Need to know for a surgery that was in April.
Omar (People Ops): Hi Sarah — sorry to hear about the surgery. We can sometimes backdate coverage for a QLE or if there was an administrative delay, but we need docs proving the spouse was eligible and that the enrollment request was timely. Did you submit within the 30-day window of the qualifying event (marriage/partner date)?
Sarah: The marriage was 2026-03-20 and I submitted enrollment on 2026-04-15 — within 30 days. I think the portal defaulted the start incorrectly to May. I have the portal confirmation email and the hospital bill dated 2026-04-20.
Omar (People Ops): Great, that helps. Please upload the portal confirmation and the hospital bill to your existing case in the Benefits portal or reply to the case with attachments. We'll mark it for manual review and request retroactive premium adjustment if approved.
Payroll Bot: Note: payroll retro adjustments are processed monthly and may take 1-2 pay cycles to appear; premiums will be prorated to the approved effective date.
Benefits Admin: Quick note: if the service occurred before coverage was approved, we require a medical necessity review only for certain claims; we will not guarantee claim payment — the carrier makes final determination. But we can request carrier retro coverage once docs are submitted.
Sarah: Uploaded docs to case 2026-BEN-789 just now. Thanks!
Omar (People Ops): Received. I'll escalate to benefits admin and flag for carrier retro review. Expect an update in 3 business days.
